_what: The owner's real ENSv2 delegation configuration, for the namespace UNICA will actually use.
As committed it REFUSES, and that is the correct output: `unica.eth` is not registered, so every
reading the planner needs is a reading of a chain that does not host the name yet. The refusal
names the first missing one. Fill the readings in, in the order under `_readings`, and the same
It will still say `signable: false` after that, for a second and separate reason: gas estimates
are an INPUT to this tool, gathered with eth_estimateGas once the names exist and handed back
with --gas. There is deliberately no flag that fills them in with a plausible number.
_mode: subtree: nothing below the parent is registered. The parent points at a Permissioned Resolver
the owner controls, that resolver answers for the whole subtree by wildcard, and the owner writes
every record at the subname nodes. One registry transaction, no PermissionedRegistry to deploy,
The cost, stated rather than buried: the names are SERVED, not DEFENDED. getSubregistry("unica")
stays zero, so today nobody can register a label under the parent — but the subnames are not held
by a registration either. Use "subregistry" instead when they must be owned; the planner keeps
that path in full and every one of its refusals.
_merchantOwner: In subtree mode this account must BE the owner of unica.eth. There is no name below the parent
for a separate merchant to hold, and every write lands on the parent's resolver, where authority
comes from holding roles at that resolver's ROOT_RESOURCE. Every transaction in the plan is
_resolver: The Permissioned Resolver the parent points at. It does not exist yet: ENSv2 gives a name its own
resolver proxy, and unica.eth is unregistered. Register the parent first, then read the proxy's
address off the registry and put it here. Do not guess it — an address with no code returns 0x to
every eth_call, and 0x decodes as "no roles", the safest-looking wrong answer in this interface.
_settlement: token: Circle's USDC on Ethereum Sepolia, the payout token UniswapDeployments.sol resolves for
chain 11155111. executor: the live V2 SettlementExecutor, 11,289 bytes, bound both ways to the
hook at 0x11202071DA4EB91bE3041A174d0c20fdaC0Ea0C0. Both are published as PUBLIC records on
pay.merchant.unica.eth and are the resources the agent is deliberately granted nothing at.
Confirm both from the chain before signing anything that publishes them. A payment record is
public forever from the moment it is written.
_policy: NOT IN THIS FILE, AND NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. This repository is public. The threshold, the
allocation, the reserve and the salt are the merchant's, they are held off chain, and only a
keccak commitment over them is ever published — treasury.merchant.unica.eth carries the digest
and the scheme string, never a value.
Fill these in on the owner's own machine, in an untracked copy of this file, and never commit
that copy. commitPolicy refuses to commit over a missing field, so the planner will say so.
_expiry: The owner's chosen expiry, as a uint64 seconds timestamp. It is only read by register(), which
subtree mode does not emit, so it is left null here. Supply it if you switch to subregistry mode.
_readings: Every value above is a READ against the chain, and none of them can be taken until unica.eth is
registered. `null` means unread. Unread is not the same as satisfied, and the planner refuses
rather than assuming — which is why this file refuses today.
parentTokenId               findTokenId("unica") on the ETHRegistry
0xBDC85dD5b15D7ecb354cd7cb6f2c50b4f2c4F0E2. Compare it with the
planner's own derivation rather than trusting either alone.
ownerRolesAtParent          roles(<that token id>, 0xA121e1eF…8D73) on the same registry.
MUST carry ROLE_SET_RESOLVER 0x1000000. This is the register()
one-shot seen from the other side: per-name roles can only ever be
set in the roleBitmap of register(), which for the parent has
already happened. A parent registered without this bit can never be
pointed at a resolver, and there is no repair short of losing it.
resolverCodeSize            eth_getCode(<the resolver>) length in bytes. Non-zero.
agentRootRolesAtResolver    roles(0, 0x19E56831…a7Ae) on the resolver. MUST be 0. A
ROOT_RESOURCE grant applies to every resource on the contract, so a
narrow grant on top of one is decoration.
merchantMayGrantAtAgentResource
eth_call the grant from the owner and see it accepted rather than
assuming it. A fork proved the mechanism on somebody else's
resolver proxy; the owner's own is still theirs to demonstrate.
assigneeReading             getAssigneeCount(<the agent leaf's per-key resource>, <bitmap>) on
the resolver, kept as {roleBitmap, counts, maxima} — the contract
returns counts AND maxima, packed one nybble per role in the same
positions as the bitmap asked about. A reading taken for a different
role does not satisfy the grant.
_beforeSigning: 1. The plan broadcasts nothing. Nothing in this repository holds a key, and no file here names a
writing JSON-RPC method — there is a scanner in the suite that fails if one ever does.
2. Read the preview row by row. The two flags — whether an admin role is involved and whether
ROOT_RESOURCE is involved — are recomputed from each row's own calldata, not copied from what
the step claims about itself, and they are printed on every row including where they are false.
3. Step 1 is skippable if the parent already points at this exact resolver. Read getResolver first.
4. The delegation is one key, one account, one leaf, and the revocation is built at the same
moment and held. A plan with no prepared revocation is never signable.
